title: task-inline-format — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one case of the Myne dialect's inline task-field extension (dialect/src/lezer/task-field.ts, taskFields.ts and taskFieldWriter.ts in the main myne repository; markdown-dialect.md §3.8). Myne READS three dialects — Obsidian's emoji markers, Obsidian's Dataview-style bracketed fields, and Myne's own key names — and WRITES one. A case therefore carries three layers: expected_dialect_spans (which UTF-8 byte ranges are recognized as which node, pre-order), expected_fields (the single typed record all three dialects collapse into), and expected_emitted_utf8_hex (the whole line as Myne would write it, since editing any field converts the whole line). Byte offsets rather than code-unit indices are load-bearing here: every emoji marker is a surrogate pair in UTF-16 and four bytes in UTF-8. An 'inert' case is a near-miss the recognizer must NOT claim. Not an on-disk codec and not cryptographic — deterministic cross-client behaviour: a port that types a value Myne refuses, or drops a field Myne preserves, silently loses user data. TS-runner category (no Rust generator).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'task-inline-format/v0.1/<slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

case_kind.description: Which surface the case exercises. dataview/emoji/myne: one of the three read dialects. mixed: both forms on one line (a half-migrated vault). preserve: a field recognized but never typed, kept verbatim. malformed: a value that must NOT type and must NOT be corrected. inert: a near-miss the recognizer must not claim (spans empty).

input_markdown_utf8_hex.description: The source line as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). The byte sequence is the contract, immune to JSON-tooling normalization.

informational_markdown.description: Human-readable mirror of input_markdown_utf8_hex; the runner cross-checks it byte-equal against the hex.

expected_dialect_spans.description: The recognized task-field spans in document (pre-order) traversal order, as UTF-8 byte offsets. Empty for inert cases.

node.description: The recognized node name. TaskFieldMark appears only in the bracketed form ('[', '::', ']'); the emoji form has no marks.

expected_fields.description: The typed record. Absent fields are OMITTED rather than null, so a port with its own optional representation does not have to invent a null encoding to agree. A value that does not type never appears here as a typed field — it appears in `malformed`.

repeat.description: The recurrence rule expression, verbatim. Its vocabulary is pinned by the separate `task-recurrence` category, not here.

priority.description: One of the five levels, whether it arrived as a word or as a priority marker emoji (where the marker IS the value).

preserved.description: Fields recognized but NOT typed by Myne — Obsidian's scheduled/start/cancelled/created/id/dependsOn, `onCompletion`, and any other inline field on the line. Kept so a whole-line rewrite cannot destroy data Myne did not understand. `onCompletion` in particular is carried and assigned no meaning whatsoever.

malformed.description: Supported keys whose value did not type — an impossible date, a UTC offset, an unknown priority word. Preserved verbatim and surfaced as unparsed: a silently shifted due date is worse than one shown as raw text.

expected_emitted_utf8_hex.description: The whole line as Myne writes it, as exact UTF-8 bytes (hex). Editing any field converts the ENTIRE line into the emitted form — bracketed fields with Myne's key names, single-space separated, in the stable order due, priority, remind, repeat, done, then preserved, then malformed. A line already in the emitted form is a FIXED POINT: re-emitting it changes nothing, which is what keeps opening a vault from dirtying its task lines.

informational_emitted.description: Human-readable mirror of expected_emitted_utf8_hex; the runner cross-checks it byte-equal against the hex.

instant.description: A local wall-clock instant. NO UTC offset and NO IANA zone identifier is ever carried: '09:00' means 09:00 wherever the user is, and a value bearing an offset does not type at all rather than being silently shifted.

date.description: A full-date that must be a REAL calendar date; 2026-02-31 passes the shape and is still refused.

time.description: Optional wall-clock time, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS.

key.description: The canonical key. Case-folded on read; Obsidian's `completion` folds onto Myne's `done`.

raw.description: The whole matched field, verbatim from the source — which differs between the two read dialects ('[due:: X]' versus the emoji form) and is therefore worth pinning.
